title: Find it or develop it

paper.title: Implicit theories of interest: Finding your passion or developing it?

thesis: Hard does not mean you picked the wrong thing. Finish the session anyway.
rule: This week, when the side project gets dull or hard, treat that as the development process. Not as evidence you found the wrong passion. Finish the session anyway.
voiceLabel: espeak-ng en-us. Placeholder TTS. Not Perk. Not a clone. Not a human host. Cairn is the body.
description: Cairn explains why a dull Thursday is not proof he picked the wrong passion. Warrant: O’Keefe, Dweck & Walton, 2018, Psychological Science.

hook.caption: Tuesday it felt like a calling.
hook.vo: Tuesday it felt like a calling.

rule.caption: Put the stone on the pile.
rule.vo: Put the stone on the pile.

scenes.caption: TUESDAY
scenes.vo: Tuesday it felt like the one. Cairn sat down and treated the pile like a calling. The files were open. The chair was in. Thursday the same pile felt like homework. Same desk. Same files. Different verdict. Cairn almost walked. Hard must mean he picked the wrong thing. It does not. Hard does not mean you picked the wrong thing. Finish the session anyway. The spark dying is the job, not the warning. That sentence has a theory inside it. Cairn will name it. Then he will stay.

scenes.label: Fixed interest
scenes.caption: Cairn treats a dull Thursday as proof he picked wrong.
scenes.vo: Part one. Fixed interest. Cairn treats a dull Thursday as proof he picked wrong. If the pile feels like homework, the passion must be fake. So Cairn closes the folder. He tells a friend it was not the one. That is the trap. A hard night is not a verdict. Find your passion is a fixed theory of interest. It makes Cairn loyal until the spark dies, then it makes him leave. Tuesday was allowed to feel like a calling. Thursday is not allowed to feel like work. He does not ask what the pile needs. He asks whether he is still the kind of person who loves this. That question is the trap. He names the theory that is talking. Fixed interest. Then he sits back down. The folder stays on the desk. The chair stays pulled in.

scenes.label: Interests develop
scenes.caption: An interest is grown. It is not found.
scenes.vo: Part two. Interests develop. An interest is grown. It is not found like a coin under a bench. When Cairn sits with a mismatching article, a find theory cools him. A develop theory keeps him curious. Same page. Different theory. Different heat. Thursday feeling like homework is not a broken compass. It is the first hour of development. Cairn does not need a new passion. He needs another pass. He does not open a new folder to feel Tuesday again. Develop it means stay long enough for the interest to thicken. Cairn gives the pile a second hour before he gives it a funeral. He talks to himself like the develop group. The article can be wrong for his taste and still be worth a pass. Taste is not a locked door.

scenes.caption: An easy Hawking video. Then a hard article.
scenes.vo: They hooked people with an easy Stephen Hawking video about black holes. Then they handed them a hard science article on the same thing. Cairn knows that move. Spark first. Then the wall. The find group cooled. The grow group stayed. You take some time, you hit a wall, over time you build that commitment. That is the story. Not a hobbyist who found the wrong craft. Hawking first. Then the hard page. Cairn stays for the hard page.

scenes.note: Cairn points at the gap. The grow-it side stayed warmer.
scenes.vo: When the article was hard, interest sat at two point seven five versus three point five nine. Cairn points at the number. The grow it side stayed warmer. The gap was biggest for people who found the article hard.

scenes.note: Stanford. Same pattern. Cairn reads the number.
scenes.vo: Five experiments. About four hundred seventy people. Stanford. Same pattern. Matching stuff feels great. Mismatching stuff dies faster if you think passion is a find. Cairn reads the number. He does not invent a hobbyist. The warrant is a set of studies, not a fable about someone who picked pottery then quit.

scenes.label: Hard is not wrong
scenes.caption: Hard does not mean Cairn picked the wrong thing.
scenes.vo: Part three. Hard is not wrong. This is the thesis as a named part. Hard does not mean Cairn picked the wrong thing. Finish the session anyway. When the side project gets dull, Cairn used to treat that as evidence. He closed the lid. That sentence felt honest and it was the fixed theory talking. Urging people to find their passion can put all the eggs in one basket, then drop the basket when it gets heavy. Cairn will not drop this basket tonight. A heavy paragraph is not a sign to switch lives. It is a sign to keep the hands on the work. Hard is a load. Wrong is a verdict. Cairn carries the load. He does not issue the verdict. If a friend asks whether this is still the one, Cairn answers with the session, not with the mood.

scenes.quote: You put all your eggs in one basket, then drop the basket when it gets heavy.
scenes.caption: Eggs in one basket. Then you drop it.
scenes.vo: The researchers said you put all your eggs in one basket, then drop the basket when it gets heavy. Cairn watches the eggs hit the floor. That is the whole warning in one picture.

scenes.label: Finish the session
scenes.caption: Cairn finishes the block he already started.
scenes.vo: Part four. Finish the session. This is the do-this move. Cairn sets a finish line he can see from the chair. One session. Not a new identity. Not a rebrand. When the spark dies, Cairn finishes the block he already started. He does not hunt a cleaner calling on the same night. He does not ask the room whether he is still passionate. He asks what the next stone is. Then he does that stone. The session ends when the block ends, not when the feeling ends. Develop it is a verb he can do before bed. Twenty minutes. One paragraph. The win is the ended block. Not a restored crush. Cairn can keep a promise to a pile.

scenes.label: Stone on the pile
scenes.caption: Cairn puts the finished block on the stack.
scenes.vo: Part five. Put the stone on the pile. Cairn takes the finished block and puts it on the stack. The pile is the record. Not the mood. Not the Tuesday glow. A stone is a session that happened. Cairn can see it. Tomorrow the pile is still there even if Thursday comes back. That is the point of a cairn. Marks on a path. Not proof of a soulmate. Cairn does not need a new species of work. He needs another stone. Mood lies. The pile does not. He leaves the room with a taller cairn than he entered.

scenes.caption: The stone leaves the hand.
scenes.vo: Cairn takes the stone out of his hand and puts it on the pile. That height is the only proof he trusts after a cold Thursday. Finish the session. Put the stone on the pile.

items: One extra test with older adults did not show the same dip.
A useful push, not a law.
scenes.vo: Mostly college students. One extra test with older adults did not show the same dip. Cairn believes the pattern. He does not pretend it is a law.

scenes.title: Hard does not mean you picked the wrong thing.
scenes.vo: Tuesday felt like the one. Thursday felt like homework. Hard is not wrong. Finish the session. Put the stone on the pile. Cairn finishes the session anyway.
